title: Rework TLS/crypto surface into modular abstraction and migrate JWT verifier incrementally
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: multiple runtime services call OpenSSL and several language bindings directly which makes upgrading or applying mitigations (CVE patches, FIPS builds) risky and error-prone. We also run three distinct JWT/OAuth verifier implementations across services (python-pyjwt, java-jose, and a lightweight Go verifier) with inconsistent JWK caching, key-rotation semantics, and error handling. Goal: introduce a small, well-tested TLS/CryptoAbstraction interface and a compatibility shim that allows us to build against OpenSSL 1.1 and OpenSSL 3 in CI, plus a staged migration of service-specific JWT adapters to a shared verifier library that centralizes JWK fetching, caching, verification, and audit hooks. The work reduces blast radius for future TLS/crypto upgrades, standardizes JWT error semantics, and closes several transitive dependency vectors for SAML/XMLSec and older OAuth clients.
acceptance_criteria: A TLS/CryptoAbstraction interface exists with a Go and Python implementation behind it
A compatibility shim allows CI to build and run unit tests against OpenSSL 1.1 and OpenSSL 3 without source changes to callers
At least three services (api-gateway, auth-service, console-proxy) have switched to the shared JWT verifier behind a feature flag
JWK cache invalidation and rotation tests cover the drift case and are added to CI
No increase in 99th percentile token-verification latency after migration (±5%)
Security review completed and SRE runbook for rollback and emergency patching exists
steps: Design crypto abstraction: define minimal surface for TLS context, signature verify, symmetric ops, and random bytes
Implement Go CryptoAbstraction with OpenSSL shim and fallback to BoringSSL build for Dedicated infra
Implement Python wrapper that reuses the Go verifier via a thin gRPC/HTTP adapter for parity tests
Extract JWT verification logic into org-shared verifier library (lang-specific bindings) with JWK fetcher + LRU cache
Add comprehensive unit and fuzz tests focusing on malformed JWTs, alg=none, key mismatch, and expiry edge cases
Create CI matrix to run builds/test suites against OpenSSL 1.1.1k and OpenSSL 3.2 images
Canary rollout: toggle feature-flag per-service, monitor token errors, latencies, and CPU/GPU crypto usage
Complete security review (Threat model + SBOM) and update SRE rollback runbook
